title: System Bus
body:
Comprised of Wires, (adsress, memory and control)

Three groups, and what each does:

| Bus | Direction | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| **Address** | CPU out | Which location is being talked to; its width sets how much memory is addressable |
| **Data** | Both ways | The value being read or written; its width is the machine's word size |
| **Control** | Both ways | Read/write, timing, bus request and grant, and the [[IRQs|IRQ]] lines |

Everything hangs off the same wires, so a [[Decoder]] on the high address bits decides
which chip responds: RAM, [[ROM]], or an [[I-O Interface]]. Under [[Memory Mapping]] the
[[CPU]] cannot tell the difference, which is the whole convenience of it.

Only one device can drive the bus at a time, which is why [[Direct Memory Access]] needs to
request it and why the [[System Controller]] exists to arbitrate.
